extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology closeout; claims are bounded to source-supported structural/phenotypic context and do not promote direct molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TP1-TP5 were predicted/modelled as amphipathic alpha-helical piscidin peptides; this is structural context, not direct killing-mechanism evidence.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Helical-wheel/structural modelling does not prove a direct antimicrobial mechanism.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=14:Structural model analysis of Nile tilapia piscidins

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TP3 and TP4 showed phenotype-level antibacterial activity in MIC assays; TP1, TP2, and TP5 did not show antibacterial activity in Table 1.
mechanism_claims.limitations: MIC activity supports antimicrobial phenotype but not a direct membrane or intracellular target mechanism.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=16:Antimicrobial spectrum of Nile tilapia piscidins and hemolytic activity

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TP2, TP3, and TP4 showed fish erythrocyte hemolysis, while TP1 and TP5 did not at 100 µg/ml; this is host-cell toxicity/context evidence.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Hemolysis indicates host-cell membrane toxicity context and is not assigned as direct antimicrobial mechanism.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=16:Antimicrobial spectrum of Nile tilapia piscidins and hemolytic activity

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TO2 cell viability results show dose-dependent cell-proliferation effects for TP3/TP4 and limited effect for TP1/TP2/TP5 at 100 µg/ml, but exact panel values were not tabulated in extracted text.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Cell viability/proliferation results are toxicity or host-cell context, not a direct AMP killing mechanism.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=17:Effects of piscidins on the viability of fish cell lines

caution_findings.detail: No pore-formation, membrane permeabilization, or intracellular target assay was performed for TP3/TP4 in this paper.
